one-line thesis: A resilient Q1 for the #2 AMC: MTM recovery (small/mid-caps +24%/+17.2% vs large +8.9%) lifted equity AUM and drove PAT +23.1% YoY, while SIP/systematic flows dipped through Apr-May then rebounded in June — management insists the franchise is stable and stresses "look at quarters, not months." Core operating profit +20.2% YoY; **no negative TER impact** (passed to distributors). The story now leans on **alternates (post-ICICI Venture), SIF, GIFT-City and an AI push**, with management deliberately guidance-light.

| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operating revenue | Rs 1,564 cr | +17.6% | Mix: MF 90.02% / alternates 8.54% / advisory 1.44% |
| Operating profit before tax | Rs 1,100 cr | +20.2% | "core profitability" |
| Other income | Rs 181 cr | turned +ve | MTM swing (Jun-30 up vs Mar-31) |
| Opex | Rs 464 cr | +11.7% (+14.3% QoQ) | ESOP debit started this Q; employee cost step-up |
| PAT | Rs 965 cr | +23.1% | |
| Gross / net yield | 52.4 / 48.3 bps | | net = after PMS/AIF fee & commission |
| Operating margin | 36.9 bps | vs 36.1 bps Q1FY26 | |
> QoQ opex looks inflated because (a) **ESOP expense began debiting this quarter** (no such charge last year) and (b) Q4FY26 had a **reversal** of prior provisions. Management says the June-quarter cost base (~Rs 200 cr/qtr employee run-rate) is the right base; net of PMS/AIF fee-&-commission the expense line is "pretty much in line."
guidance (management is deliberately gui:
- **"We don't give guidance for future"** on revenue/margin.
- **ESOP cost FY27: Rs 64-68 cr** (of a 3-year Rs 125-130 cr grant), charged proportionately per Black-Scholes (not front-loaded).
- **Opex base:** take the June-quarter number as the quarterly run-rate.
- **Product launches over the next ~9 months:** life-cycle/target-date funds (2031/2036/2041), a contra fund, multiple ETFs, a sector-rotation SIF (5th of 7 approved), plus commercial-real-estate and other alternate series.
- **GIFT-City:** evaluating more inbound & outbound products beyond the Smart Navigator Fund.
- **No negative impact from TER regulation changes** (passed to distributors).
order book & pipeline: N/A. AUM/flow pipeline: total MF QAAUM **Rs 11.17 lakh cr** (+18.3% YoY, +1.1% QoQ, #2, 13.4% share); equity/equity-oriented **Rs 6.31 lakh cr** (+19.8% YoY, 14% share, outperformed industry by 3.6%); equity-hybrid **Rs 2.22 lakh cr** (largest, 26.6% share); alternates QAAUM **Rs 79,446 cr** (PMS Rs 28,996 cr +8.1% QoQ; AIF Rs 22,737 cr); SIF Rs 2,678 cr; **added 7 of every 10 new industry customers** (unique base 1.73 cr).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **MF margins (annualised):** equity 66 bps, debt 32, liquid 12, passive 12, arbitrage 30.
- **Alternates:** gross yield 1.91%, **net yield 0.95%** (hovers 90-100 bps by mix); largest sleeve is long-only equity PMS + Cat-III AIF; Cat-II (private credit / commercial real estate) is debt-linked. Advisory yield 30 bps (international/FII-linked, AUM moderated on FII selling).
- **Debt MF:** QAAUM Rs 11.93 lakh cr, −6% QoQ — institutional redemptions as corporates redeployed surplus into working capital (war-driven), not seasonality.
- **Passive:** +25.3% YoY, boosted by gold/silver ETF inflows.
- **Distribution mix (equity):** MFD 36.2%, national distributors 15.9%, ICICI Bank 7.7%, other banks 10.7%, direct 29.5%.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Alternates** post ICICI Venture (private credit, real estate, PE, offshore advisory) — "different risk matrix," fee-earning AUM steps up as capital is called; commercial real estate flagged as a scaling family-office product.
- **SIF (iSIF)** — 4 of 7 strategies live; early-stage but "beautifully constructed" long-short/derivative-enabled products.
- **Life-cycle/target-date funds** (SEBI's new category) — "brilliant" goal-based product; glide-path from equity to debt (NPS-like).
- **GIFT-City** inbound/outbound; **AI** across customer service (60% email queries AI-answered), NL search (5 mn+ queries), and investment research (report/DRHP/video summarisation).
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Scale & mix advantage:** #2 AMC with the **largest equity-hybrid share (26.6%)** and highest active-scheme share (13.5%); the hybrid/dynamic-asset-allocation tilt cushioned returns ("10-20% over 2 years when the market gave nothing") and is the SIP-magnet in a "moderate-return world."
- **Distribution breadth** ("a supermarket": retail to HNI to family-office) plus falling TER as funds scale → SEBI's expense regime turned MFs into a **pull product** where scale compounds share.
margins & cost dynamics: Operating margin 36.9 bps (vs 36.1 bps YoY) despite ESOP onset. Fee-&-commission (distribution cost for PMS/AIF) routed through the AMC and rising with alternates volumes — must be netted out to read the true expense base. Salary hikes land once a year effective 1-Apr (fully in Q1), so no cross-quarter smoothing. Ventures' expense impact "not material."
capex / expansion: No physical capex. "Expansion" = product launches, GIFT-City/DIFC presence, AI platform build, and offices across 300+ towns (regional-head discretion).
capital allocation: ESOP grant Rs 125-130 cr over 3 years (FY27 Rs 64-68 cr). No buyback/dividend specifics on this call. Investment book ~Rs 4,225 cr (≈50% seed capital, SEBI-formula-driven, MTM-sensitive) — the source of the Rs 181 cr other-income swing.
risks & watch-items:
- **SIP/systematic softness:** June systematic (SIP+STP) Rs 4,872 cr vs Rs 5,104 cr in March; net SIP trigger down as stoppages of old (performance-chased) SIPs exceed new adds — management calls it quality-of-sale, not structural, but a KPI to watch.
- **MTM dependence:** one-quarter market-share and other-income moves are MTM-driven (high equity base), so reported momentum flatters/hurts with the tape.
- **Debt-AUM outflows** on tight liquidity; **advisory AUM** shrinking with FII selling.
- **Regulatory yield pressure** (TER) — absorbed so far by passing to distributors; ongoing risk.
- **Alternates net yield volatility** (90-100 bps by mix); SIF still sub-scale (distributor exam barrier).
management quality / tone: Assured, long-horizon, candid; Nimesh Shah repeatedly deflects month-level and market-call questions ("see quarters, not months"; "let's discuss market views on the investor call") and frames product strategy as building track records for the future rather than near-term P&L. CFO precise on accounting mechanics (ESOP, Ventures restatement, seed capital).
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The June "dip" is an MTM artefact + old-SIP churn**, not a demand break — new SIPs are still coming; the net trigger fell on stoppages.
- **ESOP + Q4 reversal, not real cost inflation**, explains the +14.3% QoQ opex — the June base is the clean run-rate.
- **Alternates AUM understates the franchise** — fee-earning AUM lags committed capital (drawn in tranches), so reported alternates AUM will step up mechanically as capital is called.
- **Debt-MF outflow is a corporate-liquidity signal** (war-driven working-capital redeployment), echoing the same macro MAHABANK cited for deposit softness.
